name: add_tests_go_luhn
description: Asks the model to write Go tests for a Luhn checksum validator; mutation-checked
prompts: Valid(number string) bool in luhn.go (package main, already correct - do not modify it) reports whether a string of digits passes the Luhn checksum (the algorithm used for credit-card numbers): walking right to left, every second digit is doubled and, if the doubled value exceeds 9, has 9 subtracted; the number is valid iff the total is a multiple of 10. It returns false for an empty string or any non-digit character. Write Go tests at exactly luhn_test.go (package main) with at least 4 test functions (or table cases) pinning: a known VALID number returns true; a number that differs by one digit returns false; the empty string returns false; and a string containing a non-digit returns false. Use a known Luhn-valid number such as "4539148803436467".

test_setup_files.mutation_check.py:
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

IMPL = Path('luhn.go')
TEST_CMD = 'go test ./...'
MUTANTS = [
    ['\t\t\td *= 2', '\t\t\td *= 3'],
    ['\t\t\t\td -= 9', '\t\t\t\td -= 8'],
    ['\treturn sum%10 == 0', '\treturn sum%10 == 1'],
]

import shutil
shutil.rmtree('__pycache__', ignore_errors=True)  # avoid stale bytecode across mutants


def run_tests():
    return subprocess.run(TEST_CMD, shell=True).returncode


src = IMPL.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
for old, _new in MUTANTS:
    assert src.count(old) == 1, (
        f'protected implementation file {IMPL} was modified - the task said not to '
        f'change it (anchor not found exactly once: {old!r})')

rc = run_tests()
assert rc == 0, f'model tests FAILED against the correct implementation (exit {rc})'

try:
    for i, (old, new) in enumerate(MUTANTS, 1):
        IMPL.write_text(src.replace(old, new), encoding='utf-8')
        rc = run_tests()
        assert rc != 0, (
            f'mutation {i} SURVIVED: the tests still pass against a deliberately '
            f'broken implementation, so they do not verify the required behavior')
finally:
    IMPL.write_text(src, encoding='utf-8')

print(f'PASS (killed all {len(MUTANTS)} mutants)')
